resources.string: This will print your robot\'s position to telemetry while allowing robot control through a basic mecanum drive on gamepad 1.
Pull your robot forward %f inches. Your forward ticks to inches will be shown on the telemetry.
The multiplier will display what your forward ticks to inches should be to scale your current distance to %f inches.
Pull your robot to the right %f inches. Your strafe ticks to inches will be shown on the telemetry.
The multiplier will display what your strafe ticks to inches should be to scale your current distance to %f inches.
Turn your robot %f radians. Your turn ticks to inches will be shown on the telemetry.
The multiplier will display what your turn ticks to inches should be to scale your current angle to %f radians.
The robot will run at 1 power until it reaches %f inches forward.
Make sure you have enough room, since the robot has inertia after cutting power.
After running the distance, the robot will cut power from the drivetrain and display the forward velocity.
Press B on game pad 1 to stop.
Press A to set the Forward Velocity temporarily (while robot remains on).
The robot will run at 1 power until it reaches %f inches to the left.
After running the distance, the robot will cut power from the drivetrain and display the strafe velocity.
Press A to set the Lateral Velocity temporarily (while robot remains on).
The robot will run forward until it reaches %f inches per second.
Then, it will cut power from the drivetrain and roll to a stop.
Make sure you have enough room.
After stopping, the forward zero power acceleration (natural deceleration) will be displayed.
Press A to set the Forward Zero Power Acceleration temporarily (while robot remains on).
The robot will run to the left until it reaches %f inches per second.
After stopping, the lateral zero power acceleration (natural deceleration) will be displayed.
Press A to set the Lateral Zero Power Acceleration temporarily (while robot remains on).
This will activate the translational PIDF(s)
The robot will try to stay in place while you push it laterally.
You can adjust the PIDF values to tune the robot\'s translational PIDF(s).
Push the robot laterally to test the Translational PIDF(s).
This will activate the heading PIDF(s).
The robot will try to stay at a constant heading while you try to turn it.
You can adjust the PIDF values to tune the robot\'s heading PIDF(s).
Turn the robot manually to test the Heading PIDF(s).
This will run the robot in a straight line going %f inches forward.
The robot will go forward and backward continuously along the path.
This will activate all the PIDF(s)
The robot will go forward and backward continuously along the path while correcting.
You can adjust the PIDF values to tune the robot\'s drive PIDF(s).
This will run the robot in a curve going %f inches to the left and the same number of inches forward.
The robot will go continuously along the path.
Driving away from the origin along the curve?: %b
This will run in a roughly triangular shape, starting on the bottom-middle point.
So, make sure you have enough space to the left, front, and right to run the OpMode.
This will run in a roughly circular shape of radius %f, starting on the right-most edge.
So, make sure you have enough space to the left, front, and back to run the OpMode.
It will also continuously face the center of the circle to test your heading and centripetal correction.
